streams.status_detail: PR #82 merged into main as a19252bb4df28e2733b6b5180c8938792c040e63. Its exact-head quality CI 45875671834 and actual CPU-thread workflow 45875671867 both succeeded. The verifier checks a strict canonical checkpoint payload, detached Ed25519 signature against caller-supplied trusted keys, expected store identity, and local event-chain hash/count; it rejects lower generations and same-sequence equivocation and marks bootstrap-only verification explicitly when no trusted high-water state is supplied. The caller must atomically persist returned state outside the SQLite rollback domain. Post-merge main quality CI 45875861427 and Pages build/deploy 45875861440 succeeded. No production signer, external high-water authority, authorized sensor/lab dataset, site-approved Water Safety Plan limits or field validation exists.
streams.next_step: Obtain independent security review of the signed checkpoint protocol and bootstrap/store-identity binding; then design an atomic high-water adapter only within a separately administered trust domain. In parallel, seek explicitly authorized paired sensor/laboratory data and site-approved Water Safety Plan limits before any preregistered field evaluation.

streams.status_detail: PR #81 merged into main as a69c3f29a7dec0f25f3a30c60f2d9f4d671807c7. Its exact-head quality CI 45872887590 and actual CPU-thread workflow 45872887552 both succeeded. The archived second raw-report set from workflow 45867519546 was rechecked: archive hashes and decompressed report hashes matched the frozen metadata, and scripts/reproduce_noema005_threaded_reruns.py --check reproduced all per-case accuracy counts and aggregate ranges. In that archived run, Neumaier-state median speedup was 0.7744x (range 0.7225–0.7935) with GIL and 1.0181x (range 0.7023–1.135) on free-threaded CPython; the prior free-threaded run was 0.9519x. The crossing of 1.0 is run-to-run variability, not evidence of a robust speedup. Both archived runs used the same hosted x86-64 runner family with 4-CPU affinity and synthetic cancellation fixtures. The study remains preliminary; representative application workloads, independent physical hardware and external numerical-method review remain outstanding. A memory-backed native benchmark protocol and C/OpenMP implementation are added on branch research/noema005-memory-bandwidth-2026-11-26; the 96 MiB buffer is reused across naive, long-double and Neumaier serial/OpenMP cases. No benchmark result is claimed yet; the exact-head workflow artifact and report validation are pending. A hosted memory-backed run is frozen: 96 MiB input, 15 serial/OpenMP cases, 1/2/4/8 native threads. Neumaier-state accuracy was 5/5 at 2/4/8 workers; four-thread median speedup was 2.351x versus serial Neumaier on this single x86_64 hosted run. Artifact ZIP and raw report digests were verified; exact tested head and raw samples are preserved. This is preliminary and not independent hardware replication.
streams.next_step: Repeat the protocol at a second buffer size and on independently selected physical x86_64 and ARM64 machines; add a representative scientific workload and hardware memory counters where available, then request independent numerical-method review.

streams.status_detail: PR #62 merged the UNDRR MHEWS 2026 country-level snapshot and arithmetic. PR #68 merged as f12a116c86514994ec40c4a953ba6a4f0a4656fc; exact-head quality CI 45849048113 succeeded. The new WMO 2026 roadmap snapshot reproduces 20/35 = 57.1429% of 35 government-validated roadmaps with clear budget allocations and approximately USD 69 million mean among those 20. An aggregate-only action-readiness validator and strict schema now keep endpoint receipts separate from survey-based receipt, comprehension, feasible action, self-reported action and verified action. Synthetic tests only; no field data, local effectiveness measurement or causal claim. Post-merge main CI 45850024686 passed 354 tests and Pages build/deploy 45850024682 succeeded.

methodology: SQLite official file-format და WAL documentation-ის მიხედვით file header-ის byte 18/19 შემოწმება
synthetic database backup/restore round-trip, WAL-mode negative case, tampered audit და no-overwrite regression tests
GitHub Actions-ის exact-head CI და mergeability verification
შემდგომ ეტაპზე encrypted off-host backup, retention/rotation და scheduled restore drills
On POSIX, stage each local SQLite snapshot in a fresh 0700 directory with a 0600 temporary database file; verify both permissions at the atomic no-overwrite publication boundary.

The restore-drill CLI requires an existing database, verifies it, creates an online SQLite snapshot and restores it into a second new path inside a temporary directory; it compares job/audit counts and the final audit-chain hash, confirms the backup bytes remain unchanged, and emits aggregate-only JSON without job IDs or payloads.
Define a strict JSON Schema 2020-12 metadata envelope for future off-host backups; tests enforce closed object boundaries and exclude secret/credential fields.
Validate proposed backup manifests with an executable JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validator and strict format checking; keep cryptographic and provider checks explicitly out of scope.

Validate the strict manifest schema, then stream plaintext and ciphertext artifacts through SHA-256 and byte-length checks using one file descriptor; reject non-regular files, symlinks where O_NOFOLLOW exists, and obvious file mutation during hashing.

Runtime exact-byte Ed25519 detached-signature verification against caller-supplied trusted public keys, followed by streamed plaintext/ciphertext SHA-256 and byte-length checks; synthetic ephemeral-key tests only.

data_needs: synthetic SQLite databases with rollback-journal and WAL header states
backup/restore test fixtures and immutable source hash
CI job logs and exact commit SHA
Operator-approved non-production database for a real restore drill; record elapsed time and aggregate recovery evidence only.
risks: immutable=1 SQLite connection may mask the stored WAL journal mode
same-host backup does not protect against host/disk loss
backup is currently unencrypted and has no off-host retention automation
audit hash chain without signed external checkpoint does not prevent all tampering scenarios
Private staging-directory permissions are POSIX-specific; the final backup remains subject to the destination parent's ACL and can be exposed if that parent is too permissive.

The restore-drill CLI validates a same-host temporary filesystem round-trip only; it does not validate encrypted off-host storage, provider object versions, key recovery or clean-host disaster recovery.
A matching unsigned manifest and matching artifact hashes do not authenticate provenance; an attacker able to replace both files and the manifest can recompute the hashes.
A valid detached signature does not prove that a signed backup is the newest; rollback/freeze protection requires separately trusted monotonic state and freshness policy.
The local verifier authenticates exact manifest bytes only when the caller's public key is independently trusted; key compromise, revocation and rotation are not managed here.
blockers: No production backup encryption/decryption pipeline or off-host storage provider is configured.
Signing-key custody, rotation/revocation, threshold policy and independently trusted public-key provisioning remain unapproved and undeployed.

Rollback-resistant high-water state, immutable object-version/retention verification, clean-host restore, approved RPO/RTO and production ACLs remain unimplemented; no operator-approved deployed/staging database has been used.
streams.status_detail: Main contains local strict manifest/schema validation, streamed artifact digest/length checks and exact-byte Ed25519 verification using caller-supplied public keys. PR #85 is a separate draft architecture proposal for a provider-neutral linearizable compare-and-advance high-water authority and explicit restore lineage; its exact-head quality CI 45876372188 and CPU-thread workflow 45876372172 succeeded, but the PR is not merged and no service is deployed. Production anti-rollback, key custody, immutable object retention, off-host encryption and clean-host restore remain unimplemented.
streams.next_step: Obtain independent security/architecture review and an owner for the separate trust domain and recovery path. Only then implement a provider-neutral CAS interface with deterministic concurrent-writer, stale-state, timeout and point-in-time restore tests; choose provider, RPO/RTO and retention with explicit owner approval. Do not create a Supabase project or reuse another project's database.
success_metrics: backup includes committed WAL data
restore rejects WAL-mode header and corrupted audit data before destination creation
restore never overwrites an existing destination and does not mutate source bytes
complete unit tests, frozen research reproductions, site build and publication-boundary checks pass
restore drill and encrypted off-host backup policy are documented and later independently tested
On POSIX, a test observes the staging directory at 0700 and the SQLite snapshot at 0600 immediately before no-overwrite publication, even when the destination parent is 0777.
restore-drill returns success only when source and restored databases are valid, job/audit counts and final audit hash match, and the backup bytes remain unchanged
restore-drill output contains aggregate metadata only and explicitly identifies the same-host-only evidence boundary
The future manifest is structurally validated against a strict schema; every object rejects unlisted fields and no secret/private-key material is permitted.
Runtime manifest validator accepts a synthetic schema-valid document and rejects malformed hashes, invalid UTC timestamps, missing fields and secret-like extra properties.
No claim of off-host disaster-recovery readiness until a clean-host restore is independently attested against approved RPO/RTO.

The verifier accepts only when both plaintext and ciphertext SHA-256 digests and byte lengths match the strict manifest; missing, modified, non-regular, symlink (where supported) and concurrently changing artifacts fail closed.
A synthetic manifest signature verifies only against an independently supplied trusted public key and exact manifest bytes; tampering, unknown signer and duplicate JSON keys fail closed.
Both local artifact hashes and byte lengths match the signed manifest before verification succeeds.
No claim of newest-backup or rollback protection until monotonic trusted state and freshness policy are independently persisted and tested.
No production disaster-recovery readiness claim until encrypted off-host artifacts are restored on a clean host against approved RPO/RTO.
